ko.L: 명절의 마지막 날, 곧 큰 [날에] 예수께서 서서 외쳐 말씀하셨다. "누구든지 목마르면, 나에게 와서 마셔라.
ko.B: 명절의 마지막 날, 가장 큰 날에 예수께서 서서 큰 소리로 말씀하셨다. "목마른 사람은 누구든지 나에게 와서 마셔라.
ko.R: 명절의 마지막 날이었다. 그날은 명절에서 가장 중요한 날이었다. 예수께서 일어서서 사람들에게 큰 소리로 말씀하셨다. "목마른 사람은 누구나 나에게 와서 마셔라.

decisions.choice: the last day, the great day of the feast: the close of the Festival of Tabernacles
alternatives: the seventh day, the last of the seven days of the feast
the eighth day, the closing day of solemn assembly
decisions.reason: The feast is Tabernacles (Booths), named in 7:2. The law sets seven days of the feast and then an eighth day of solemn assembly (Leviticus 23:34-36; Numbers 29:35). John does not say whether "the last day" is the seventh day or that eighth day; both were high points. The sense of the sentence is the same either way.

decisions.choice: thirst and drink: an invitation set against the water of the feast
decisions.reason: During Tabernacles, according to the Mishnah (Sukkah 4:9, written down about AD 200 and describing practice in the temple before its fall), a priest drew water from the Pool of Siloam each morning of the feast and poured it out at the altar. Tabernacles was also linked with prayer for rain and with Zechariah 14:8, 16-17, where living waters flow out from Jerusalem and the nations come up to keep the feast. Jesus's call also echoes God's invitation in Isaiah 55:1, "Come, everyone who thirsts, come to the waters", and his words to the Samaritan woman about living water (4:10-14). The connection with the water rite is likely but not stated by John.

decisions.choice: stood and cried out: a loud, public announcement
decisions.reason: Teachers usually sat to teach (Luke 4:20; Matthew 5:1). Here Jesus stands and cries out, the verb John uses for a solemn public declaration (1:15; 7:28; 12:44). It marks what follows as a proclamation to the whole festival crowd.

decisions.choice: {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}, {{deity_pronoun:his|His}}, {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}, {{deity_pronoun:you|You}}
decisions.reason: Every pronoun for Christ or for God uses the deity_pronoun setting, including "me" and "my" when Jesus speaks of himself and "you" when people speak to him. At the start of a sentence "He" is written plain. This applies throughout the passage.

decisions.choice: {{gender:them|him}} (L); {{gender:they|he}} (B, R)
decisions.reason: "Anyone" means any person, man or woman, so the pronoun that takes it up has the gender setting. Balanced and Readable say "should come" for the command form "let him come", which is stiff in modern English, and "is thirsty" for "thirsts".

decisions.choice: no gender setting
decisions.reason: Spanish says "que venga" with no pronoun for "anyone", so no setting is needed.

decisions.choice: narration in the passé simple (L, B), with Literal keeping John's present tense (7:50 "dit"); passé composé (R); speech in the passé composé at every level
alternatives: passé composé for narration at every level
the present tense throughout at Literal
decisions.reason: The French brief for the whole passage (7:37-52), as in 1:19. The passé simple ("s’écria", "répondirent") is the normal tense of written narrative; Readable uses the passé composé ("a crié", "ont répondu"). In 7:50 John says "says"; Literal keeps the present, which for "dire" has the same form as the passé simple ("il dit"), while Readable writes "a dit". Speech uses the passé composé at every level.

decisions.choice: no gender setting: "qu’il vienne" after "quelqu’un" (L, B); "Tous ceux qui ont soif" (R)
decisions.reason: English puts the pronoun under the gender setting. French "il" taking up "quelqu’un" is grammatical agreement with an indefinite pronoun and is read as "anyone", as in 7:17; a doubled "il ou elle" would weigh down a short invitation. Readable uses the plural, which is plainly general.

decisions.choice: "ai" with no gender span
alternatives: a gender span as in the English
decisions.reason: "ai" (anyone) needs no following pronoun in Vietnamese and is already inclusive, so the gender setting has nothing to change. The same holds in 7:46 and 7:51.

decisions.choice: No deity_pronoun spans in Korean
alternatives: capitalised pronoun spans as in English
decisions.reason: Korean has no capital letters, so the reader setting has nothing to change. Respect for Jesus is carried by the subject honorific ("-시-", "께서") and "그분" in the narrative at every level; Jesus himself speaks in the plain style (해라체) as everywhere in the book. This holds for the whole passage.

decisions.choice: No gender span: "누구든지 ... 와서 마셔라"
alternatives: a gender setting span as in English
decisions.reason: Korean addresses the invitation to "anyone" without a pronoun, so it already includes everyone and the gender setting has nothing to change.

source.text: ὁ πιστεύων εἰς ἐμέ, καθὼς εἶπεν ἡ γραφή, ποταμοὶ ἐκ τῆς κοιλίας αὐτοῦ ῥεύσουσιν ὕδατος ζῶντος.

records.literal_gloss: The [one] believing in me, as said the Scripture, rivers out of the belly of him will flow of water living."

en.L: The one who believes in {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}, as the Scripture said, 'Out of his belly will flow rivers of living water.'"
en.B: As for the one who believes in {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}, it is just as the Scripture said: 'Rivers of living water will pour out from deep within him.'"
en.R: It is just as the Scripture says: rivers of living water will flow from deep inside the one who believes in {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}."

es.L: El que cree en {{deity_pronoun:mí|Mí}}, como dijo la Escritura: “De su vientre correrán ríos de agua viva”».
es.B: Al que cree en {{deity_pronoun:mí|Mí}}, como dijo la Escritura: “De lo más profundo de su ser brotarán ríos de agua viva”».
es.R: Es tal como dice la Escritura: ríos de agua viva brotarán de lo más profundo del que cree en {{deity_pronoun:mí|Mí}}».

fr.B: Pour celui qui croit en {{deity_pronoun:moi|Moi}}, c’est comme l’a dit l’Écriture : “Des fleuves d’eau vive jailliront du plus profond de son être.” »

sw.L: Anayeniamini {{deity_pronoun:mimi|Mimi}}, kama Andiko lilivyosema, 'Mito ya maji yaliyo hai itatiririka kutoka tumboni mwake.'"
sw.B: Kuhusu yule anayeniamini {{deity_pronoun:mimi|Mimi}}, ni kama Andiko lilivyosema: 'Mito ya maji yaliyo hai itabubujika kutoka ndani kabisa mwake.'"
sw.R: Ni kama Andiko linavyosema: mito ya maji yaliyo hai itatiririka kutoka ndani kabisa ya mtu anayeniamini {{deity_pronoun:mimi|Mimi}}."

vi.L: Người tin vào {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}}, như Kinh Thánh đã nói: 'Từ trong lòng người ấy sẽ tuôn chảy những dòng sông nước sống.'"
vi.B: Ai tin vào {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} thì như Kinh Thánh đã nói: 'Những dòng sông nước sống sẽ tuôn chảy từ sâu thẳm trong lòng người ấy.'"
vi.R: Đúng như Kinh Thánh nói: những dòng sông nước sống sẽ chảy ra từ sâu trong lòng người tin vào {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}}."

ko.L: 나를 믿는 사람은, 성경이 말한 대로, '그의 배에서 살아 있는 물의 강들이 흘러나올 것이다.'"
ko.B: 나를 믿는 사람은, 성경이 말한 대로 '그 속 깊은 곳에서 생수의 강들이 흘러나올 것이다.'"
ko.R: 성경에서 말한 것처럼, 나를 믿는 사람의 마음 깊은 곳에서 생명을 주는 물이 강물처럼 흘러나올 것이다."

decisions.choice: a full stop after "drink" (7:37): the rivers flow from the one who believes
alternatives: a comma after "to me": "let him come to me, and let the one who believes in me drink"; the rivers flow from Christ
decisions.reason: The manuscripts have no punctuation, so the words can be divided two ways. The SBLGNT ends the sentence at "drink" and begins a new one with "the one who believes in me", which then names the person from whose inmost being the rivers flow. The other way joins "the one who believes in me" to the call before it: "If anyone thirsts, let him come to me, and let the one who believes in me drink." Then the rivers flow from Christ himself, and the two lines balance neatly; 19:34, where water flows from his side, and the rock that gave water in the wilderness (Exodus 17:6; 1 Corinthians 10:4) are often brought in on that side. On the SBLGNT side, 4:14 says that the water Jesus gives becomes in the one who drinks "a spring of water welling up", and the sentence reads naturally as it stands. Both readings agree that the living water is the Spirit (7:39) and that its source is Jesus; they differ on whom "his" means in the quotation. We follow the SBLGNT; a footnote gives the other reading.

decisions.choice: belly: the inmost being of a person
decisions.reason: The word means the belly or womb, and in biblical Greek it often stands for the inner self, the place of a person's deepest life and feelings. The picture is of water pouring out from the very center of someone. On the SBLGNT punctuation "his" is the believer (meaning decision m1); on the other reading it is Christ.

decisions.choice: as the Scripture said: a summary of several passages, not one verse
decisions.reason: No Old Testament verse has these words. Passages that come close are Isaiah 58:11 ("like a spring of water whose waters do not fail"), Isaiah 44:3 (water poured on the thirsty land, God's Spirit poured out), Ezekiel 47:1-12 (a river flowing from the temple and giving life), Zechariah 14:8 (living waters flowing out from Jerusalem, read at Tabernacles), and the water from the rock in the wilderness (Exodus 17:6; Psalm 78:16). Jesus seems to gather the sense of these rather than quote one of them. Which passages are chiefly in mind is uncertain.

decisions.choice: living water: flowing water, and water that gives life
decisions.reason: "Living water" was the ordinary term for running water from a spring or stream, as against still water in a cistern. As at 4:10-14, Jesus uses it of the life he gives, and 7:39 says what it means: the Spirit.

decisions.choice: his, him: no setting
decisions.reason: The pronoun is left plain, with neither the gender setting nor the deity_pronoun setting, because either one would decide whom it refers to, the believer or Christ (meaning decision m1). Literal keeps "belly"; Balanced says "from deep within", which is what the word means here (meaning decision m2).

decisions.choice: rivers of living water will flow from deep inside the one who believes in me
decisions.reason: Readable turns the hanging phrase into a plain sentence and names the believer as the one from whom the water flows, following the reading the text adopts (meaning decision m1). The footnote there gives the other reading.

decisions.choice: su, no setting
decisions.reason: As in English, the pronoun is left plain, since either setting would decide the question of meaning decision m1. Spanish "su" is the same for him or her.

decisions.choice: vientre (L); lo más profundo de su ser (B, R)
decisions.reason: The word means the inmost being (meaning decision m2); Literal keeps "vientre".

decisions.choice: eau vive
decisions.reason: French "eau vive" is the ordinary term for running spring water and at the same time says "living", so it holds both senses of meaning decision m4, as at 4:10.

decisions.choice: son ventre (L); son être (B): no setting
decisions.reason: As in English, the possessive is left plain, since a deity_pronoun setting would decide that the rivers flow from Christ, not from the believer (meaning decision m1). French "son" does not mark gender, so no gender setting arises.

decisions.choice: lòng
decisions.reason: Vietnamese "lòng" is both the belly and the inmost self, so Literal can keep the Greek picture without the crudeness of "bụng" and Balanced needs no explanation.

decisions.choice: "살아 있는 물" (L); "생수" (B); "생명을 주는 물" (R)
decisions.reason: "생수" is the familiar Bible word, but in everyday Korean it now means bottled mineral water. Literal keeps the image of living, flowing water; Balanced keeps the familiar word; Readable says what the water does.

source.text: τοῦτο δὲ εἶπεν περὶ τοῦ πνεύματος οὗ ἔμελλον λαμβάνειν οἱ πιστεύσαντες εἰς αὐτόν· οὔπω γὰρ ἦν πνεῦμα, ὅτι Ἰησοῦς οὐδέπω ἐδοξάσθη.

records.literal_gloss: This now he said about the Spirit whom were about to receive the [ones] having believed in him; not yet for was Spirit, because Jesus not yet was glorified.

en.L: Now {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} said this about the Spirit, whom those who believed in {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} were about to receive; for [the] Spirit was not yet [given], because Jesus was not yet glorified.
en.B: He was speaking about the Spirit, whom those who believed in {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} were soon to receive. The Spirit was not yet given, because Jesus had not yet been glorified.
en.R: Jesus was talking about the Spirit. People who believed in {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} would receive the Spirit later. At that time the Spirit had not yet been given, because Jesus had not yet been glorified. That would happen through {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} death on the cross and {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} return to the Father.

es.L: Esto dijo acerca del Espíritu, que habían de recibir los que creyeran en {{deity_pronoun:él|Él}}; pues el Espíritu aún no [había sido dado], porque Jesús aún no había sido glorificado.
es.B: Hablaba del Espíritu, que pronto recibirían los que creyeran en {{deity_pronoun:él|Él}}. El Espíritu todavía no había sido dado, porque Jesús todavía no había sido glorificado.
es.R: Jesús hablaba del Espíritu. Los que creían en {{deity_pronoun:él|Él}} recibirían el Espíritu más tarde. En ese momento el Espíritu todavía no había sido dado, porque Jesús todavía no había sido glorificado. Eso sucedería por medio de su muerte en la cruz y su regreso al Padre.

fr.L: Or {{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} dit cela au sujet de l’Esprit que devaient recevoir ceux qui avaient cru en {{deity_pronoun:lui|Lui}} ; car [l’]Esprit n’était pas encore [donné], parce que Jésus n’avait pas encore été glorifié.
fr.B: Il parlait de l’Esprit que ceux qui croyaient en {{deity_pronoun:lui|Lui}} allaient bientôt recevoir. L’Esprit n’avait pas encore été donné, parce que Jésus n’avait pas encore été glorifié.
fr.R: Jésus parlait de l’Esprit. Ceux qui croyaient en {{deity_pronoun:lui|Lui}} allaient recevoir l’Esprit plus tard. À ce moment-là, l’Esprit n’avait pas encore été donné, parce que Jésus n’avait pas encore été glorifié. Cela allait se passer par {{deity_pronoun:sa|Sa}} mort sur la croix et {{deity_pronoun:son|Son}} retour auprès du Père.

sw.L: Basi alisema hivi kuhusu Roho, ambaye wale waliomwamini walikuwa karibu kumpokea; kwa maana Roho alikuwa bado [hajatolewa], kwa sababu Yesu alikuwa bado hajatukuzwa.

sw.R: Yesu alikuwa akizungumza kuhusu Roho. Watu waliomwamini wangempokea Roho baadaye. Wakati huo Roho alikuwa bado hajatolewa, kwa sababu Yesu alikuwa bado hajatukuzwa. Hilo lingetokea kupitia kifo {{deity_pronoun:chake|Chake}} msalabani na kurudi {{deity_pronoun:kwake|Kwake}} kwa Baba.

vi.L: Ngài nói điều ấy về Thánh Linh mà những người tin vào {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} sắp nhận lãnh; vì Thánh Linh chưa [được ban], bởi Đức Giê-xu chưa được tôn vinh.
vi.B: Ngài nói về Thánh Linh, Đấng mà những người tin vào {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} sắp nhận lãnh. Bấy giờ Thánh Linh chưa được ban xuống, vì Đức Giê-xu chưa được tôn vinh.
vi.R: Đức Giê-xu nói về Thánh Linh. Những người tin vào {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} sau này sẽ nhận được Thánh Linh. Lúc ấy Thánh Linh chưa được ban cho, vì Đức Giê-xu chưa được tôn vinh. Việc ấy sẽ xảy ra khi {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} chịu chết trên thập tự giá và trở về với Cha.

ko.L: 그런데 그분께서 이것을 말씀하신 것은, 그분을 믿은 사람들이 받게 될 성령에 대해서였다. 아직 성령이 [주어지지] 않았는데, 예수께서 아직 영광을 받지 않으셨기 때문이다.
ko.B: 이것은 그분을 믿는 사람들이 곧 받게 될 성령을 두고 하신 말씀이었다. 예수께서 아직 영광을 받지 않으셨으므로, 성령이 아직 주어지지 않았던 것이다.
ko.R: 예수께서는 성령에 대해 말씀하신 것이다. 예수님을 믿는 사람들은 나중에 성령을 받게 될 것이었다. 그때는 아직 성령이 주어지지 않았다. 예수께서 아직 영광을 받지 않으셨기 때문이다. 그 일은 예수께서 십자가에서 돌아가시고 아버지께로 돌아가실 때 이루어질 것이었다.

decisions.choice: for the Spirit was not yet (SBLGNT)
alternatives: for the Spirit was not yet given
for the Holy Spirit was not yet
for the Holy Spirit was not yet given
decisions.reason: The SBLGNT reads simply "for the Spirit was not yet". Many manuscripts add a word to make the sense plain: some read "given", some "holy" ("the Holy Spirit was not yet"), and some have both ("the Holy Spirit was not yet given"). The additions explain the short reading rather than change its sense (meaning decision m2). Reviewers should check the evidence against the apparatus.

decisions.choice: the Spirit was not yet: not yet given to believers
decisions.reason: John does not mean that the Spirit did not exist: the Spirit came down on Jesus at his baptism (1:32-33). He means that the Spirit had not yet been given to those who believe. Jesus later promises to send the Spirit after he goes away (14:16-17, 26; 16:7), and after the resurrection he breathes on his disciples and says, "Receive the Holy Spirit" (20:22).

decisions.choice: glorified: Jesus's death, resurrection and return to the Father
decisions.reason: In John, Jesus is glorified in his "hour", his death on the cross together with his rising and his return to the Father (12:16, 23-24; 13:31-32; 17:1, 5). Until then the Spirit could not be given (16:7). The word is the key term "glorify".

decisions.choice: the narrator explains, looking back
decisions.reason: This verse is John's own comment, as at 2:21-22 and 12:33: he tells the reader what Jesus meant. "Those who believed in him" are all who came to believe; "were about to receive" looks ahead from the time of the story to the giving of the Spirit after Easter.

decisions.choice: [given] (L); given (B, R)
decisions.reason: English cannot say "the Spirit was not yet" without seeming to deny that the Spirit existed, which John does not mean (meaning decision m2). Every level supplies "given", the sense the context requires; Literal puts it in brackets.

decisions.choice: That would happen through his death on the cross and his return to the Father.
decisions.reason: Readable says what "glorified" refers to here (meaning decision m3), since a young reader would not know. It keeps the word "glorified" itself.

decisions.choice: [había sido dado] (L); había sido dado (B, R)
decisions.reason: As in English: Spanish cannot say "the Spirit was not yet" without seeming to deny that the Spirit existed (meaning decision m2).

en.R: Some of the people in the crowd heard what Jesus said. They said, "This man really is the Prophet God promised to send!"

vi.B: Có những người trong đám đông nghe những lời ấy thì cứ nói: "Ông này thật là Đấng Tiên Tri."
vi.R: Có những người trong đám đông nghe Đức Giê-xu nói như vậy. Họ bảo: "Người này thật đúng là Đấng Tiên Tri mà Đức Chúa Trời đã hứa sai đến!"

ko.L: 그러자 무리 가운데 이 말씀들을 들은 [어떤 이들은] 말하고 있었다. "이 사람은 참으로 그 예언자이다."
ko.B: 이 말씀을 들은 무리 가운데 어떤 사람들은 "이 사람은 정말 그 예언자이다." 하고 말했다.
ko.R: 무리 가운데 어떤 사람들은 예수님의 말씀을 듣고 "이 사람은 하나님께서 보내겠다고 약속하신 바로 그 예언자이다!" 하고 말했다.

decisions.choice: the Prophet: the prophet like Moses promised in Deuteronomy 18:15-18
decisions.reason: God promised Moses to raise up a prophet like him (Deuteronomy 18:15-18), and by Jesus's time some expected this Prophet as a figure of the last days (1:21, 25; 6:14). After the feeding, people said the same thing (6:14). Here the talk of water may have reminded them of Moses, who gave Israel water from the rock (Exodus 17:6), but John does not say so.

decisions.choice: some of the crowd were saying: ongoing talk among different groups
decisions.reason: "Of the crowd" means some of them; 7:41 goes on to others with other views. The verb "were saying" describes talk going on through the crowd, not one shout.

decisions.choice: these words: Jesus's call in 7:37-38
decisions.reason: The words that set the crowd talking are the invitation to come and drink and the promise of living water.

decisions.choice: the Prophet, with a capital
decisions.reason: As at 1:21 and 6:14, the capital shows that a particular expected figure is meant, not any prophet. Readable says who he is (meaning decision m1): the crowd's own term meant the Prophet God had promised, so this adds nothing they did not know.

decisions.choice: el Profeta, with a capital
decisions.reason: As at 1:21 and 6:14: a particular expected figure.

decisions.choice: Đấng Tiên Tri
decisions.reason: The Prophet like Moses is a promised figure, so the title is capitalised and takes the respectful "Đấng"; "Vị Tiên Tri" is a little less weighty and may suit a reviewer better, since the speakers do not yet see him as divine.

decisions.choice: "그 예언자"
decisions.reason: "예언자" is the current everyday word; "선지자" is the older church word many readers know. "그" marks the one promised prophet, as the article does in Greek; Korean has no capital to do it.

en.R: Other people said, "He is the {{christos:Christ|Messiah}}!" But some said, "The {{christos:Christ|Messiah}} is not supposed to come from Galilee!

sw.R: Watu wengine walisema, "Yeye ndiye {{christos:Kristo|Masihi}}!" Lakini wengine walisema, "{{christos:Kristo|Masihi}} hapaswi kutoka Galilaya!

vi.L: Người khác nói: "Người này là {{christos:Đấng Christ|Đấng Mê-si-a}}." Nhưng có người lại nói: "Chẳng lẽ {{christos:Đấng Christ|Đấng Mê-si-a}} lại đến từ Ga-li-lê sao?
vi.B: Người khác nói: "Ông này là {{christos:Đấng Christ|Đấng Mê-si-a}}." Nhưng có người phản đối: "Lẽ nào {{christos:Đấng Christ|Đấng Mê-si-a}} lại xuất thân từ Ga-li-lê?
vi.R: Người khác nói: "Ông ấy là {{christos:Đấng Christ|Đấng Mê-si-a}}!" Nhưng có người nói: "{{christos:Đấng Christ|Đấng Mê-si-a}} đâu có đến từ Ga-li-lê!

ko.L: 다른 이들은 "이 사람은 {{christos:그리스도|메시아}}이다." 하고 말하고 있었다. 그러나 어떤 이들은 말하고 있었다. "{{christos:그리스도|메시아}}께서 갈릴리에서 나오시겠느냐?
ko.B: 또 어떤 사람들은 "이 사람은 {{christos:그리스도|메시아}}이다." 하고 말했다. 그러나 어떤 사람들은 반대했다. "{{christos:그리스도|메시아}}께서 설마 갈릴리에서 나오시겠느냐?
ko.R: 다른 사람들은 "이 사람은 {{christos:그리스도|메시아}}이다!" 하고 말했다. 그러나 어떤 사람들은 이렇게 말했다. "{{christos:그리스도|메시아}}께서는 갈릴리에서 나오실 리가 없다!

decisions.choice: a question expecting the answer no, voiced with disbelief
decisions.reason: The question is shaped to expect "no": the speakers take it for granted that the Christ does not come from Galilee. The small word "for" ties it to the claim just made: "[He cannot be,] for surely the Christ does not come from Galilee?"

decisions.choice: from Galilee: where Jesus was known to come from
decisions.reason: Jesus was known as "Jesus of Nazareth" (1:45-46), a town in Galilee, and he had spent most of his time there. The objectors assume that this settles where he is from. Others in Jerusalem expected that no one would know where the Christ comes from (7:27); the crowd is divided even about what to expect.

decisions.choice: the Christ: the anointed king Israel was waiting for
decisions.reason: "Christ" means "anointed one" (1:41), the king from David's line promised in the Scriptures. Some think Jesus is the Prophet (7:40), some the Christ, and some reject both; John lays out the views side by side, and 7:43 sums them up as a division.

decisions.choice: the {{christos:Christ|Messiah}}
decisions.reason: A title with the article, so every level writes "the" outside the span, as at 1:20.

decisions.choice: is not supposed to come from Galilee!
alternatives: Surely the Christ does not come from Galilee?
decisions.reason: Readable gives the answer the question expects (meaning decision m1) as a plain statement of what the speakers believed. Balanced keeps the question with "Surely".

decisions.choice: el {{christos:Cristo|Mesías}}
decisions.reason: A title with the article, as at 1:20.

decisions.choice: ¡Se supone que el Cristo no viene de Galilea!
decisions.reason: As in English: Readable gives the answer the question expects (meaning decision m1).

decisions.choice: le {{christos:Christ|Messie}}
decisions.reason: As in 1:20: a title with the article (meaning decision m3), so every level writes "le" outside the span. This applies throughout the passage.

decisions.choice: viendrait-il (donc) ... ?
alternatives: Le Christ vient-il de la Galilée ?
decisions.reason: The question expects no and is said with disbelief (meaning decision m1). The French conditional carries that disbelief; Readable gives the expected answer as a statement, as in English.

decisions.choice: The expected Christ takes the honorific ("께서 ... 나오시겠느냐"); Jesus is "이 사람"
decisions.reason: The speakers honour the Messiah they are waiting for but not the man in front of them; Korean must choose, and the contrast keeps John's irony. The christos span stands alone, since Korean has no article.

records.literal_gloss: Not the Scripture said that out of the seed of David, and from Bethlehem the village where was David, comes the Christ?"

en.L: Has not the Scripture said that out of the seed of David, and from Bethlehem, the village where David was, the {{christos:Christ|Messiah}} comes?"
en.B: The Scripture says, does it not, that the {{christos:Christ|Messiah}} comes from the family line of David, and from Bethlehem, David's own village?"
en.R: The Scripture says that the {{christos:Christ|Messiah}} will come from the family of King David. It says {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} will come from Bethlehem, the town where David lived."

es.L: ¿No ha dicho la Escritura que del linaje de David, y de Belén, la aldea donde estaba David, viene el {{christos:Cristo|Mesías}}?».
es.B: ¿No dice la Escritura que el {{christos:Cristo|Mesías}} viene de la descendencia de David, y de Belén, la aldea de David?».
es.R: La Escritura dice que el {{christos:Cristo|Mesías}} vendrá de la familia del rey David. Dice que vendrá de Belén, el pueblo donde vivió David».

fr.L: L’Écriture n’a-t-elle pas dit que c’est de la semence de David, et de Bethléem, le village où était David, que vient le {{christos:Christ|Messie}} ? »
fr.B: L’Écriture ne dit-elle pas que le {{christos:Christ|Messie}} sera de la lignée de David, et qu’{{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} viendra de Bethléem, le village de David ? »
fr.R: L’Écriture dit que le {{christos:Christ|Messie}} viendra de la famille du roi David. Elle dit qu’{{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} viendra de Bethléem, le village où David habitait. »

sw.B: Andiko linasema, sivyo, kwamba {{christos:Kristo|Masihi}} anatoka katika ukoo wa Daudi, na kutoka Bethlehemu, kijiji cha Daudi mwenyewe?"
sw.R: Andiko linasema kwamba {{christos:Kristo|Masihi}} atatoka katika jamaa ya Mfalme Daudi. Linasema kwamba {{deity_pronoun:yeye|Yeye}} atatoka Bethlehemu, mji aliokuwa akiishi Daudi."

vi.L: Chẳng phải Kinh Thánh đã nói rằng {{christos:Đấng Christ|Đấng Mê-si-a}} đến từ dòng dõi Đa-vít, và từ Bết-lê-hem, làng mà Đa-vít đã ở, sao?"
vi.B: Kinh Thánh chẳng đã nói rằng {{christos:Đấng Christ|Đấng Mê-si-a}} xuất thân từ dòng dõi Đa-vít, và từ Bết-lê-hem, làng của chính Đa-vít, đó sao?"
vi.R: Kinh Thánh nói rằng {{christos:Đấng Christ|Đấng Mê-si-a}} sẽ ra từ gia đình của vua Đa-vít. Kinh Thánh cũng nói {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} sẽ đến từ Bết-lê-hem, là thị trấn nơi Đa-vít đã sống."

ko.L: 성경이 {{christos:그리스도|메시아}}께서 다윗의 씨에서, 그리고 다윗이 살던 마을 베들레헴에서 오신다고 말하지 않았느냐?"
ko.B: 성경에 {{christos:그리스도|메시아}}께서는 다윗의 자손으로, 다윗이 살던 마을 베들레헴에서 나오신다고 하지 않았느냐?"
ko.R: 성경에는 {{christos:그리스도|메시아}}께서 다윗 왕의 집안에서 나오신다고 적혀 있다. 또 그분이 다윗이 살던 마을인 베들레헴에서 나오신다고 적혀 있다."

decisions.choice: the seed of David and Bethlehem: the promises of a king from David's line
decisions.reason: God promised David that one of his offspring would reign after him for ever (2 Samuel 7:12-16; Psalm 89:4-5; also Isaiah 11:1). Micah 5:2 says that a ruler of Israel will come from Bethlehem, small among the clans of Judah. Bethlehem was David's home town (1 Samuel 16:1-13; 17:12). "The Scripture said" sums up these passages; it does not quote one verse.

decisions.choice: irony: the speakers are sure of where Jesus is from
decisions.reason: The speakers assume Jesus comes from Galilee and so cannot be the Christ. John does not tell of Jesus's birth; readers who know Matthew 2:1-6 and Luke 2:4-7, where he is born in Bethlehem, will hear the irony. John's own concern is that they judge his origin by the wrong measure: he comes from the Father (7:28-29; 8:14). The text itself does not say more than this.

decisions.choice: the seed of David: David's descendants
decisions.reason: "Seed" is the usual biblical word for offspring, a man's descendants (as in 2 Samuel 7:12).

decisions.choice: the {{christos:Christ|Messiah}}
decisions.reason: A title with the article, so every level writes "the" outside the span, as at 1:20.

decisions.choice: family line (B); family of King David, the town where David lived (R)
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable say "family" for "seed" (meaning decision m3) and keep the question as a statement the speakers expect everyone to grant: Balanced with "does it not", Readable as a plain statement. Readable says David "lived" there for "where David was", and calls him King David for readers who do not know him.

decisions.choice: linaje (L); descendencia (B); familia (R)
decisions.reason: As in English: says what "seed" means (meaning decision m3).

decisions.choice: division: a split into opposing sides
decisions.reason: The word is used of a tear in cloth; John uses it of people who split into camps over Jesus (also 9:16; 10:19).

decisions.choice: because of him: Jesus divides people
decisions.reason: In John people are divided by how they respond to Jesus (3:19-21; 9:39). The crowd's split is not over a rule or a teaching but over who he is (7:40-42).

decisions.choice: divided into groups ... They could not agree about him.
decisions.reason: Readable names Jesus and spells out what a division was.

ko.L: 그런데 그들 가운데 어떤 이들은 그분을 잡고 싶어 했으나, 아무도 그분께 손을 대지 않았다.
ko.B: 그들 가운데 몇 사람은 그분을 붙잡아 가려고 했지만, 아무도 그분께 손을 대지 못했다.
ko.R: 그들 가운데 몇 사람은 예수님을 체포하고 싶어 했다. 그러나 아무도 예수님을 붙잡지 못했다.

decisions.choice: some of them: some of the crowd
decisions.reason: "Them" refers back to the crowd of 7:43. The officers sent to arrest Jesus (7:32) may have been among them; 7:45-46 shows they too did nothing.

decisions.choice: laid hands on him: arrested him
decisions.reason: To lay hands on someone means to seize or arrest them, as in 7:30.

decisions.choice: no one laid hands on him: his hour had not yet come
decisions.reason: John has just explained a similar failure: "no one laid a hand on him, because his hour had not yet come" (7:30; also 8:20). Here he does not repeat the reason, but the reader is meant to remember it: no one can take Jesus before the time the Father has set.

decisions.choice: take into custody (B); arrest (R)
decisions.reason: The verb means to seize, here with the aim of arresting him (7:30, 32). Balanced and Readable use the plainer words for an arrest.

decisions.choice: mit les mains sur lui (L); mit la main sur lui (B)
decisions.reason: French "mettre la main sur quelqu’un" is the same idiom as the Greek and means to seize (meaning decision m2), so Balanced keeps it, in its usual singular; Literal keeps the Greek plural.

source.text: Ἦλθον οὖν οἱ ὑπηρέται πρὸς τοὺς ἀρχιερεῖς καὶ Φαρισαίους, καὶ εἶπον αὐτοῖς ἐκεῖνοι· Διὰ τί οὐκ ἠγάγετε αὐτόν;

records.literal_gloss: Came therefore the officers to the chief priests and Pharisees, and said to them those, "Why not did you bring him?"

en.L: So the officers came to the chief priests and Pharisees, and those said to them, "Why did you not bring {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}?"
en.B: So the temple police returned to the chief priests and Pharisees, and these men asked them, "Why have you not brought {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}?"
en.R: So the temple guards went back to the leading priests and the Pharisees. The leaders asked them, "Why did you not bring {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} here?"

es.L: Vinieron, pues, los alguaciles a los principales sacerdotes y fariseos, y estos les dijeron: «¿Por qué no lo {{plural_you:trajeron|trajisteis}}?».
es.B: Entonces los guardias del templo volvieron a los jefes de los sacerdotes y a los fariseos, y estos les preguntaron: «¿Por qué no lo {{plural_you:han traído|habéis traído}}?».
es.R: Entonces los guardias del templo volvieron a donde estaban los jefes de los sacerdotes y los fariseos. Los dirigentes les preguntaron: «¿Por qué no lo {{plural_you:trajeron|trajisteis}} aquí?».

fr.L: Les gardes vinrent donc vers les chefs des prêtres et les Pharisiens, et ceux-ci leur dirent : « Pourquoi ne {{deity_pronoun:l’|L’}}avez-vous pas amené ? »
fr.B: Les gardes du temple retournèrent donc auprès des chefs des prêtres et des Pharisiens, qui leur demandèrent : « Pourquoi ne {{deity_pronoun:l’|L’}}avez-vous pas amené ? »
fr.R: Alors les gardes du temple sont retournés vers les chefs des prêtres et les Pharisiens. Ces chefs leur ont demandé : « Pourquoi ne {{deity_pronoun:l’|L’}}avez-vous pas amené ici ? »

sw.L: Basi wale watumishi walikwenda kwa wakuu wa makuhani na Mafarisayo, nao wakawaambia, "Mbona hamkumleta?"
sw.B: Basi walinzi wa hekalu walirudi kwa wakuu wa makuhani na Mafarisayo, nao wakawauliza, "Kwa nini hamkumleta?"
sw.R: Basi walinzi wa hekalu walirudi kwa viongozi wa makuhani na Mafarisayo. Viongozi wakawauliza, "Kwa nini hamkumleta hapa?"

vi.L: Vậy các cảnh vệ trở về với các thầy tế lễ cả và người Pha-ri-si, và những người ấy hỏi họ: "Tại sao các anh không giải ông ta đến?"
vi.B: Vậy lính canh đền thờ trở về với các thầy tế lễ cả và người Pha-ri-si, và các ông ấy hỏi họ: "Sao các anh không giải ông ta đến đây?"
vi.R: Vậy những người lính canh đền thờ trở về với các thầy tế lễ cả và những người Pha-ri-si. Các nhà lãnh đạo ấy hỏi họ: "Sao các anh không bắt ông ta về đây?"

ko.L: 그래서 경비병들이 대제사장들과 바리새파 사람들에게 왔고, 그들이 경비병들에게 말했다. "왜 너희는 그를 데려오지 않았느냐?"
ko.B: 성전 경비병들이 대제사장들과 바리새파 사람들에게 돌아오자, 그들이 물었다. "어찌하여 그를 데려오지 않았느냐?"
ko.R: 성전 경비병들은 대제사장들과 바리새파 사람들에게 돌아갔다. 지도자들이 그들에게 물었다. "왜 그를 여기로 데려오지 않았느냐?"

decisions.choice: the officers: the temple police
decisions.reason: These are the officers the chief priests and Pharisees sent to arrest Jesus (7:32). They served the chief priests and kept order in the temple (18:3, 12). John does not say how long it was since they were sent; 7:32 seems to fall in the middle of the feast (7:14), and this is the last day.

decisions.choice: the chief priests and Pharisees: the leaders who sat on the council
decisions.reason: The chief priests were the high priest and the leading priestly families; with leading Pharisees they made up much of the Jerusalem council. John often names the two groups together as the ones who act against Jesus (7:32; 11:47, 57; 18:3).

decisions.choice: those: the chief priests and Pharisees
decisions.reason: "Those" points to the leaders just named, who question their officers.

decisions.choice: temple guards; leading priests
decisions.reason: Readable says what the officers were and avoids "chief priests", which a young reader may not understand.

decisions.choice: guardias del templo; jefes de los sacerdotes
decisions.reason: As in 7:32.

decisions.choice: les gardes (L); les gardes du temple (B, R); les chefs des prêtres (every level)
decisions.reason: The book-wide French terms for John, as at 7:32. "Officier" is a military rank and "huissier" a court usher in today's French, so "gardes" names the temple police (meaning decision m1). "Les chefs des prêtres" is plain enough for Readable, which therefore does not need the English "leading priests".

decisions.choice: watumishi (L); walinzi wa hekalu (B, R)
decisions.reason: ὑπηρέται were the temple police who served the council. Literal says "watumishi" (attendants, officers); Balanced and Readable name them as temple guards, as the English does. "Askari" would suggest Roman soldiers.

decisions.choice: "các anh" for the officers; "ông ta" for Jesus
decisions.reason: The leaders speak down to their own guards with "các anh", which is plain without the archaic "các ngươi"; they keep calling Jesus "ông ta", with no deity_pronoun span, as opponents do through the book.

decisions.choice: các thầy tế lễ cả; cảnh vệ (L), lính canh đền thờ (B, R)
decisions.reason: "thầy tế lễ cả" is the established Protestant term for the chief priests; the officers were the temple police, named as guards at Literal and as temple guards at Balanced and Readable.

decisions.choice: "경비병들" (L); "성전 경비병들" (B, R)
decisions.reason: The temple police who served the council, as in 7:32; "하인들" (servants) would hide that they were sent to arrest him.

source.text: ἀπεκρίθησαν οἱ ὑπηρέται· Οὐδέποτε ἐλάλησεν οὕτως ἄνθρωπος.

records.literal_gloss: Answered the officers, "Never spoke thus a man."

en.L: The officers answered, "Never has {{gender:anyone|a man}} spoken like this."
en.B: The temple police answered, "No one has ever spoken like this!"
en.R: The guards answered, "We have never heard anyone speak the way {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} does!"

es.B: Los guardias del templo respondieron: «¡Nadie ha hablado nunca así!».
es.R: Los guardias respondieron: «¡Nunca hemos oído a nadie hablar como {{deity_pronoun:él|Él}}!».

fr.L: Les gardes répondirent : « Jamais {{gender:personne|un homme}} n’a parlé ainsi. »
fr.B: Les gardes du temple répondirent : « Personne n’a jamais parlé comme cela ! »
fr.R: Les gardes ont répondu : « Nous n’avons jamais entendu personne parler comme {{deity_pronoun:lui|Lui}} ! »

sw.B: Walinzi wa hekalu wakajibu, "Hakuna mtu aliyewahi kusema kama huyu!"
sw.R: Walinzi wakajibu, "Hatujawahi kumsikia mtu yeyote akisema kama yeye anavyosema!"

vi.L: Các cảnh vệ đáp: "Chưa hề có người nào nói như thế."
vi.B: Lính canh đáp: "Chưa từng có ai nói như vậy!"
vi.R: Những người lính canh trả lời: "Chúng tôi chưa bao giờ nghe ai nói như ông ấy cả!"

ko.L: 경비병들이 대답했다. "사람이 이렇게 말한 적은 한 번도 없었습니다."
ko.B: 성전 경비병들이 대답했다. "지금까지 그렇게 말한 사람은 아무도 없었습니다!"
ko.R: 경비병들이 대답했다. "우리는 그 사람처럼 말하는 사람을 한 번도 본 적이 없습니다!"

decisions.choice: Never has a man spoken like this (SBLGNT)
alternatives: Never has a man spoken as this man speaks
Never has a man spoken like this man
decisions.reason: The SBLGNT has the short reading, found in some of the earliest manuscripts. Many manuscripts read "Never has a man spoken like this man", and some add "as this man speaks". The longer readings spell out what the short one implies. Reviewers should check the evidence against the apparatus.

decisions.choice: a man: any human being
decisions.reason: The word is the general word for a human being. The officers mean that no one has ever spoken like this. The reader may hear more in it: John has shown that Jesus is more than a man (1:1, 14; 10:33).

decisions.choice: the officers came back without him because of his words
decisions.reason: Sent to arrest Jesus, the officers return empty-handed; what stopped them was the way he spoke. Their answer stands against the leaders' contempt in the next verses.

decisions.choice: {{gender:anyone|a man}}
decisions.reason: The word means any human being (meaning decision m2), so Literal has the gender setting. Balanced and Readable say "no one" and "anyone", which are already inclusive.

decisions.choice: We have never heard anyone speak the way he does!
decisions.reason: Readable says what "like this" points to: the way Jesus speaks.

decisions.choice: {{gender:nadie|ningún hombre}}
decisions.reason: The word means any human being (meaning decision m2); Balanced and Readable say "nadie".

decisions.choice: Jamais {{gender:personne|un homme}} n’a parlé ainsi
alternatives: Jamais un homme n’a parlé ainsi
decisions.reason: The word means any human being (meaning decision m2), so Literal has the gender setting, with the inclusive "personne" by default. Balanced and Readable say "personne", which is already inclusive.

decisions.choice: The officers answer their superiors in the formal polite style (합쇼체: "없었습니다")
decisions.reason: Temple police reporting to the chief priests and Pharisees speak up to them; the leaders answer in the plain style (7:45, 7:47).

decisions.choice: No gender span: "사람"
alternatives: a gender setting span as in English
decisions.reason: "사람" already means any human being, so Korean has nothing for the gender setting to change.

en.R: The Pharisees answered, "Do not tell us that {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} has fooled you too!

fr.B: Les Pharisiens rétorquèrent : « Vous ne vous êtes tout de même pas laissé berner, vous aussi ?

sw.L: Basi Mafarisayo wakawajibu, "Je, ninyi nanyi mmedanganywa?
sw.B: Mafarisayo wakawajibu kwa ukali, "Hakika ninyi hamjadanganyika pia?
sw.R: Mafarisayo wakajibu, "Msituambie kwamba amewadanganya ninyi pia!

vi.L: Vậy người Pha-ri-si đáp lại họ: "Chẳng lẽ các anh cũng bị lừa dối rồi sao?
vi.B: Người Pha-ri-si vặn lại: "Chẳng lẽ các anh cũng bị mắc lừa rồi sao?
vi.R: Người Pha-ri-si đáp: "Đừng nói là các anh cũng bị ông ta lừa rồi nhé!

ko.L: 그러자 바리새파 사람들이 그들에게 대답했다. "너희도 미혹된 것은 아니겠지?
ko.B: 바리새파 사람들이 맞받아 말했다. "설마 너희까지 넘어간 것은 아니겠지?
ko.R: 바리새파 사람들이 대답했다. "설마 그 사람이 너희까지 속인 것은 아니겠지!

decisions.choice: deceived: led astray from the truth
decisions.reason: The verb means to lead astray. It takes up what some in the crowd said of Jesus earlier, that "he leads the people astray" (7:12). The law warned against a prophet who would lead Israel astray from the Lord (Deuteronomy 13:1-5); the Pharisees treat Jesus as such a man.

decisions.choice: a question expecting no, said with scorn
decisions.reason: The question is shaped to expect "no": "Surely you too have not been fooled?" The perfect tense asks whether they are now in a deceived state. "You too" puts the officers alongside the crowd the Pharisees despise (7:49).

decisions.choice: taken in (B); fooled, with he as the one who did it (R)
decisions.reason: Everyday words for being deceived. Readable names Jesus ("he") as the one who deceived them, which the passive implies, and puts the scorn of the question into a plain exclamation.

decisions.choice: también a ustedes los ha engañado
decisions.reason: As in English: Readable makes Jesus the one who deceived them, which the passive implies (meaning decision m1).

source.text: μή τις ἐκ τῶν ἀρχόντων ἐπίστευσεν εἰς αὐτὸν ἢ ἐκ τῶν Φαρισαίων;

vi.R: Chẳng có ai trong các nhà lãnh đạo của chúng ta tin vào ông ta cả. Người Pha-ri-si cũng chẳng ai tin!

ko.L: 관리들 가운데 누가 그를 믿었느냐? 아니면 바리새파 사람들 가운데 [누가 믿었느냐]?
ko.B: 지도자들 가운데 그를 믿은 사람이 하나라도 있느냐? 바리새파 사람 가운데 하나라도 있느냐?
ko.R: 우리 지도자들 가운데 그를 믿은 사람은 아무도 없다. 바리새파 사람들 가운데도 아무도 없다!

decisions.choice: the rulers: the leading members of the council
decisions.reason: "Rulers" are the men who held authority among the people, the members of the Jerusalem council. Nicodemus is called "a ruler of the Jews" (3:1).

decisions.choice: irony: a ruler and Pharisee is about to speak up
decisions.reason: The question expects the answer "none", but at once Nicodemus, both a Pharisee and a ruler (3:1), speaks in Jesus's favor (7:50-51). Later John says that many even of the rulers believed in him, though they kept it quiet for fear of the Pharisees (12:42).

decisions.choice: a question expecting no
decisions.reason: As in 7:47, the question is shaped to expect "no". The Pharisees argue that if none of the leaders believe, Jesus cannot be what the crowd says.

decisions.choice: a single one ... a single Pharisee (B); two statements (R)
alternatives: Has any of the rulers believed in him, or of the Pharisees? (Literal)
decisions.reason: Balanced brings out the scorn of the question; Readable gives the answer the question expects, "none", as two plain statements and says "leaders" for "rulers".

decisions.choice: two statements
decisions.reason: As in English: Readable gives the answer the question expects (meaning decision m3).

vi.B: Còn đám đông này, chẳng biết gì về luật pháp, thì bị nguyền rủa."

decisions.choice: this crowd that does not know the law: the common people, looked down on by the learned
decisions.reason: The Pharisees devoted themselves to studying the law of Moses and keeping it in detail. They scorn the ordinary people, who had neither the time nor the training to do so, as ignorant of the law and therefore easily misled. Later Jewish writings show the same contempt from some teachers for "the people of the land", a phrase that in the Hebrew Scriptures simply means the population of the country. The words reveal the speakers' attitude; John does not share it.

decisions.choice: accursed: under God's curse
decisions.reason: The law pronounces a curse on anyone who does not keep its words (Deuteronomy 27:26; 28:15). The Pharisees treat the crowd's ignorance as a failure to keep the law and so place them under that curse. The irony is that in the next verses they themselves ignore what the law requires (7:51).

decisions.choice: the crowd ... are: a singular noun with a plural verb
decisions.reason: "Crowd" is singular but "are accursed" is plural: the Pharisees think of the crowd as so many people.

decisions.choice: the law of Moses; God's curse
decisions.reason: Readable says which law is meant and whose curse, both of which the Pharisees take for granted (meaning decisions m1 and m2).

decisions.choice: esta multitud ... son (L)
decisions.reason: Literal keeps the singular noun with the plural verb, as the Greek has it (meaning decision m3).

decisions.choice: la ley de Moisés; de Dios
decisions.reason: As in English: says which law and whose curse.

decisions.choice: cette foule ..., ce sont des maudits
decisions.reason: The Greek puts a singular noun with a plural verb (meaning decision m3): the crowd is thought of as many people. French "ce sont" after the singular noun does the same, as English "are" does.

decisions.choice: Nicodemus: a Pharisee and a ruler who had come to Jesus
decisions.reason: Nicodemus is the Pharisee and "ruler of the Jews" who came to Jesus by night (3:1-2). He appears once more, bringing spices for Jesus's burial (19:39). "One of them" means one of the Pharisees and rulers just mentioned; he is the answer to their question in 7:48.

decisions.choice: the one who had come to him before (SBLGNT)
alternatives: the one who had come to him by night
the one who had come to him by night before
decisions.reason: Some manuscripts read "the one who had come to him by night", and some combine the two ("by night, before"); a few leave out the description altogether. The longer readings recall 3:2 and 19:39. Reviewers should check the evidence against the apparatus.

decisions.choice: says (L); said (B, R)
decisions.reason: John tells this in the present tense ("says"), the historic present, as he often does. Literal keeps it; Balanced and Readable use the past, as English tells a story. This applies once in the passage.

decisions.choice: Jesus (for "him"); Readable: one of those Pharisees, spoke up
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable name Jesus, since "him" right after "them" could be unclear. Readable puts the description first in its own sentences and says that Nicodemus was one of the Pharisees (meaning decision m1); it does not add "by night", which is the variant reading (m2).

decisions.choice: historic present at Literal; pretérito at Balanced and Readable
decisions.reason: As elsewhere in John: Literal keeps John's present ("dice", "ven"); Balanced and Readable use the pretérito. This applies throughout the passage.

decisions.choice: Historic present kept at Literal ("말한다"); past at Balanced and Readable
decisions.reason: Korean narrative can use the present for vividness, so Literal keeps John's present tense. One decision for the passage.

decisions.choice: our law: the law's demand for a fair hearing
decisions.reason: The law of Moses tells judges to hear both sides and judge fairly (Deuteronomy 1:16-17), and to inquire carefully before condemning anyone (Deuteronomy 17:4; 19:18). Nicodemus does not quote one verse; he appeals to what the law plainly requires. The irony is sharp: the men who have just said the crowd does not know the law (7:49) are ready to condemn Jesus without hearing him.

decisions.choice: judge: pass judgment, condemn
decisions.reason: The verb means to judge, and here to judge against someone. In the setting it means to condemn Jesus without a hearing.

decisions.choice: the man: the person accused, whoever it is
decisions.reason: The article points to the person on trial in any case. The words are general, about anyone accused, though Nicodemus has Jesus in mind.

decisions.choice: a question expecting no
decisions.reason: Like the Pharisees' questions (7:47-48), Nicodemus's question expects "no": the law does not do this. He turns their own way of speaking back on them.

decisions.choice: {{gender:person|man}}, {{gender:them|him}}, {{gender:they have|he has}}
decisions.reason: The law speaks of anyone accused, man or woman (meaning decision m3), so the gender setting applies. Balanced says "anyone" and Readable "a person", which are already inclusive; the pronouns that follow carry the setting.

decisions.choice: two statements and a short question
decisions.reason: Readable states what the law requires and keeps Nicodemus's appeal to his hearers in "Is that not right?", which matches the question's expected answer.

decisions.choice: {{gender:una persona si primero no la oye|un hombre si primero no lo oye}}
decisions.reason: The law speaks of anyone accused (meaning decision m3). Literal keeps the noun with the inclusive default; the span takes in the pronoun that agrees with it. Balanced says "alguien" and Readable "la persona acusada".

decisions.choice: {{gender:la personne|l’homme}}, with the pronouns and agreements that follow under the same setting
decisions.reason: The law speaks of anyone accused, man or woman (meaning decision m3). The inclusive default says "la personne", and because the noun is feminine the pronouns and participles agree with it ("elle", "entendue", "la"); the traditional option keeps "l’homme", "il", "le".

decisions.choice: No gender spans: "사람", "본인", "그 사람"
alternatives: gender setting spans as in English
decisions.reason: Korean refers to the accused as "사람" and "그 사람" with no gendered pronoun, so the sentence already covers anyone and the setting has nothing to change.

decisions.choice: Nicodemus speaks to his fellow council members in the plain style (해라체)
decisions.reason: Among equals the style guide's default is 해라체; the council answers him in the same level (7:52).

decisions.choice: are you also from Galilee: a sneer, not a real question
decisions.reason: The question expects "no" and is meant as an insult: "Surely you are not one of those Galileans too?" They are not asking where Nicodemus was born; they are lumping him with the Galilean Jesus and his followers from the despised crowd (7:41, 49).

decisions.choice: Galilee: a region far from Jerusalem

decisions.choice: como él

decisions.choice: a prophet (SBLGNT)
alternatives: the Prophet does not arise from Galilee
no prophet has arisen from Galilee
decisions.reason: The SBLGNT reads "a prophet". The early papyrus P66, and possibly P75, has "the prophet", which would make the claim narrower: the Prophet like Moses (7:40) does not come from Galilee. Many later manuscripts also read the verb as "has arisen" instead of "arises". Reviewers should check the evidence against the apparatus.

decisions.choice: no prophet from Galilee: a claim the Scriptures do not bear out
decisions.reason: The leaders speak as if Scripture settles the matter, but the prophet Jonah son of Amittai came from Gath-hepher (2 Kings 14:25), a town in the territory of Zebulun in Galilee (Joshua 19:13). Those who scorn the crowd for not knowing the law (7:49) overlook this; John leaves the irony for the reader.

decisions.choice: search: study the Scriptures
decisions.reason: The verb is the one Jesus used in 5:39, "You search the Scriptures". The leaders tell Nicodemus to look into the written word and see for himself.

decisions.choice: the Scriptures
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable name what is to be searched, which the verb implies here (meaning decision m3). Readable says "comes from" for "arises".

decisions.choice: escudriña
decisions.reason: The verb Jesus used in 5:39, "escudriñan las Escrituras", so the link stays visible; Balanced and Readable name what is to be searched.
